findings.summary: The two new comment blocks are swapped relative to the statements they document, i.e. code executes strip-comments-then-unescape while the comments describe (and appear to have been written for) unescape-then-strip-comments.
findings.mechanism: Line 32-34's comment ("Docling's markdown export HTML-escapes... unescape... Runs before quote normalization") sits above the `re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", ...)` call on line 35, and line 36-38's comment ("Strip all HTML comments BEFORE group_broken_paragraphs") sits above the `html.unescape(text)` call on line 39. Functionally harmless for literal `<!-- image -->` placeholders, but if Docling ever entity-encodes the comment delimiters (e.g. `<!-- image -->`) in some export path, the strip regex (running before unescape, contrary to what the comments claim/imply) won't match them, and they'll fall through to `group_broken_paragraphs` unstripped — the exact shredding bug this change was written to prevent. At minimum this mismatched documentation will mislead a future maintainer about execution order.
